llm.summary: This skill is a clearly disclosed VMware audit and policy helper; it stores sensitive local audit data, but the behavior is purpose-aligned and documented.

dimensions.detail: It writes local audit, rules, and undo state under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME and inspects only the presence of a few agent-identifying environment variables; this is proportionate for audit logging but users should treat the audit database as confidential.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is declared through uv as vmware-policy==1.18.2, with no executable files bundled in the artifact; the artifact points to public source and describes manual or dependency installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It auto-loads as a dependency for the VMware skill family and affects decorated VMware tool calls, but that scope is explicitly disclosed and tied to the infrastructure role.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local SQLite audit logs and YAML rules are disclosed, permissions are documented, and there is no evidence of cron jobs, services, backdoors, or hidden persistence. Policy defaults allow operations unless the operator configures deny rules.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is audit logging, optional policy enforcement, and sanitization for VMware skills; the documented capabilities match that purpose and it exposes no MCP tools of its own.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that this skill records VMware tool activity locally, including parameters and results after best-effort redaction. Restrict access to ~/.vmware, configure deny rules for production or destructive actions, avoid leaving VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 set, and review audit exports before sending them to external systems.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig/token/password references are redaction examples for audit rows, not evidence of reading credential files.
[SQP-1] expected: Auto-loading is broad but disclosed as the infrastructure dependency for the VMware skill family.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit export is an expected compliance workflow; the artifact also warns that audit data is sensitive, though users should review exports before sharing.
[PE2] expected: The chmod examples set restrictive user-owned permissions on ~/.vmware and audit.db; they do not require sudo or root.
[RA2] expected: The persistent state is local audit/rules/undo storage needed for the stated purpose, not an unauthorized persistence mechanism.
[EA2] expected: The default policy denies nothing, but this is explicitly disclosed and positioned as optional operator policy layered on top of VMware RBAC.
[E3] expected: The ls command is a scoped troubleshooting check for ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, not broad filesystem enumeration.
